Requirements: Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended; Letters of Recommendation (the number required varies by program); A Statement of Academic Purpose (required for all programs); Test Scores (GRE, English Language Tests, etc.); Writing Sample (if required by your program); Résumé/CV (if required by your program); Application Fee

The online application form, along with the application fee, is typically the first step. You will then be asked to upload or submit additional materials as outlined below. Always refer to your desired program's page for specific details, as requirements may vary.

Transcripts: Unofficial transcripts from each college or university where you have earned a degree, or from which you have received credit for courses that you wish to have count toward your graduate degree at NYU, are required for the application process. Official transcripts will be required upon admission.

Letters of Recommendation: Most departments require three letters of recommendation from faculty or others qualified to evaluate your academic and professional abilities. Please consult the specific program to which you are applying for further details on the number of letters and the type of information that is expected. Recommenders upload their letters directly to the online application system.

Statement of Academic Purpose: This required statement should be a concise essay of approximately 500 words (or two pages double-spaced) that describes your primary academic and research interests, your experiences, and your objectives.

Resume/Curriculum Vitae: Required for all applicants.

Test Scores:
GRE General Test: Many departments require the Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) General Test. Some departments require a GRE Subject Test. For master's programs in the sciences and social sciences, the GRE General Test may be optional or required. Please check your desired program's page for specifics.
English Language Proficiency Test: All applicants are required to demonstrate proficiency in English to be considered for admission. Proficiency can be demonstrated in one of the following ways: TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, or PTE Academic, or by meeting exemption criteria.

Writing Sample: Required only by specific programs. Please consult the specific program to which you are applying for further details.

The application process for the Full-time MBA program at NYU Stern requires an online application, essays (two short essays and one professional aspirations essay), a resume, academic transcripts from all prior institutions (self-reported initially), GMAT/GRE/Executive Assessment (EA) scores (waivers may be available for eligible candidates), two letters of recommendation (at least one from a current or former supervisor), a video essay, and an application fee ($250, fee waivers available for some applicants). Applicants whose native language is not English and who have not completed their undergraduate or graduate degree in an institution where the sole language of instruction is English must also demonstrate English Language Proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS required).

Upload all of the following in the application portal: Statement of Purpose (500 words or less), Resume/CV, Two (2) Letters of Recommendation, Academic Transcripts, Portfolio (see below for specific requirements), GRE is not required, English Language Proficiency (if applicable). All applicants must apply online through the NYU Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS) website.

Online Application
You will submit the online application where you will upload the following:
*   Resume: Upload your most current professional resume, including your work history, education, volunteer work, and extracurricular activities.
*   Essays: Answer the essay questions provided in the online application. We learn more about your unique personality, professional goals, and decision-making skills through these essays.
*   Letters of Recommendation: You will be required to submit two letters of recommendation. One letter must be from a current or previous supervisor. The second letter may be from an additional supervisor, or someone who can speak to your professional strengths, such as a client or a professor.
*   Transcripts: Upload unofficial transcripts from all colleges and universities you have attended in the education section of the online application. If admitted, official transcripts from all degree-granting institutions will be required.
*   Standardized Tests (GMAT/GRE): The GMAT or GRE is required for all applicants. An official GMAT or GRE score report is required by the application deadline. Please have your official scores sent to NYU Stern using the following codes: GMAT (ZT2-R0-38) and GRE (2582). Stern does not have a minimum score requirement. Waiver for CPA-Eligible Applicants: Applicants who have passed all four sections of the CPA exam may be eligible for a GMAT/GRE waiver. More information regarding the waiver and eligibility criteria is available in the online application.
*   Application Fee: A $120 non-refundable application fee is required and must be paid online via credit card. Waivers are available in specific circumstances, including U.S. military personnel and members of certain organizations.

Complete and submit the online application. Pay the non-refundable application fee. Unofficial transcripts are required for the application review process. Official transcripts are required upon admission. English language proficiency is required for international students whose native language is not English. These should attest to your clinical competence, academic ability, and potential for leadership. Referees will receive an email from NursingCAS with instructions on how to submit letters on your behalf; A current resume or curriculum vitae (CV); A personal statement (500 words maximum) outlining your professional goals and reasons for pursuing graduate study in your chosen specialization; A copy of your current, active, and unencumbered RN license(s) from the state(s) in which you plan to complete your clinical hours. All applicants must submit an online application, application fee, unofficial transcripts from each college or university attended, letters of recommendation (most departments require three), a Statement of Purpose, a resume or curriculum vitae, and the GRE General Test (required for Computer Science MS applicants). All applicants must submit their applications through the GSAS online application system. The Computer Science Department does not waive this requirement. All applicants must complete the online application. We require the following documents: Unofficial transcripts are required for the application process. Official transcripts are required upon admission. Two letters of recommendation are required from faculty members or employers familiar with your academic or professional capabilities. A one-page essay describing your academic and career goals and how a graduate degree from NYU Tandon will help you achieve them. Resume/CV is required. The GRE General Exam is optional for all MS programs for Spring 2024, Fall 2024, and Spring 2025. English Language Proficiency is required for international applicants if their native language is not English and they have not completed a baccalaureate or master's degree at an institution where the sole language of instruction is English. Accepted tests include TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, and PTE Academic.

An undergraduate degree in engineering, architecture, construction management, or a related field (such as technology or science) from an accredited institution. Applicants with an undergraduate degree in other areas such as business or liberal arts will be considered providing they have sufficient technical work experience. Minimum 3.0 GPA. Official TOEFL / IELTS score, if applicable.

Applications for Executive Certificate programs are open on a rolling basis. To apply, simply fill out the Executive Certificate Application and provide a copy of your resume. Candidates must have at least five years of experience in construction or a related field. No prerequisites are required.

All applicants are required to submit an application and the following supporting documents: an official copy of your undergraduate transcript showing a minimum GPA of 3.0 (applicants with a lower GPA will be considered for admission on a case-by-case basis), a resume, and an essay. International applicants must also submit official proof of English language proficiency (official credential evaluations are not required). The essay should be approximately 250 words, describing interest in the program, goals, and how prior academic/professional experience has prepared them. A current resume detailing academic and professional accomplishments must be submitted. Official transcripts from all previously attended undergraduate and graduate institutions are required; electronic transcripts are preferred and can be sent to sps.admissions@nyu.edu.

Transcripts, Two Letters of Recommendation, Resume/CV, Statement of Purpose, GRE Scores (optional). International applicants may be required to submit proof of English proficiency. See additional requirements for international applicants.

Requirements: The general PhD program application requirements at NYU Steinhardt are: A completed online application, Application fee, Academic transcripts, Resume/CV, Statement of Purpose, Letters of recommendation (3), GRE General Test (Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical Writing scores), Writing Sample, English Language Proficiency Testing (for international applicants). For the Counseling Psychology PhD program, the GRE General Test is Required. For the Statement of Purpose, please address the following prompts as well as the general Statement of Purpose guidelines, in approximately 750-1000 words: Your significant life and work experiences related to your interest in Counseling Psychology, your proposed area of research, and career goals; Your specific research interests and a research question you would like to explore; Why you are interested in the Counseling Psychology PhD program at NYU Steinhardt and how you see our program as a good fit for your scholarly and professional development; One or two faculty members whose research is aligned with your interests and why you would like to work with them.

Completed online application form (including basic information, educational history, extracurricular activities, awards, and distinctions), Statement of Purpose, Resume/C.V., Official Transcripts (from all colleges/universities attended), Two Letters of Recommendation, Writing Sample, TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test Scores (if applicable).

A completed online application form. Academic Transcripts from all previously attended colleges and universities. Two Letters of Recommendation. Statement of Purpose. Resume or CV. GRE Scores (see GRE Requirements page to determine if your program requires the GRE). English Language Proficiency (if applicable). Application Fee.

Two letters of recommendation. GRE general test scores are NOT required for applicants to the Biology MS program.

Application Fee, Academic Transcripts, 3 Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose, Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV), GRE General Test (optional for all doctoral programs), English Language Proficiency Test (if applicable).

Official Transcripts, Statement of Purpose, Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV), and Letters of Recommendation are required. English Language Testing is required for international applicants unless they meet specific criteria. The GRE General Test is not required.

Online Application, Application Fee, Official Transcripts from each college or university attended, Resume/CV, Statement of Purpose (a one-page approximately 500 words describing academic and professional qualifications and goals for graduate study), Two (2) Letters of Recommendation (three preferred for doctoral applicants), GRE General Test (optional for all master’s programs for Fall 2024, Spring 2025, Fall 2025, Spring 2026), and English Language Proficiency Requirement (TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo) for international applicants whose native language is not English and who have not received a bachelor’s or master’s degree from an institution where the sole language of instruction is English.

Applicants to all GSAS programs must submit a complete application online. The GRE General Test is required; the GRE Subject Test in Mathematics is strongly encouraged but not required. English Language Proficiency must be demonstrated if your native language is not English and your undergraduate institution is not in a country where English is the sole official language of instruction. Prerequisites include a strong background in mathematics, including advanced calculus, linear algebra, probability, and statistics; some prior exposure to financial mathematics or economics is helpful but not strictly required.

General application requirements for admission to the Graduate School of Arts and Science, including an online application, application fee, academic transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, three letters of recommendation, a curriculum vitae/resume, a statement of academic purpose, and GRE General Test scores. English language testing is required for international applicants unless exempt.

Applicants are generally required to submit unofficial transcripts from each college or university attended, a Statement of Purpose, three Letters of Recommendation, GRE General Test scores (no waivers), and an application fee. English Language Proficiency scores (TOEFL/IELTS) are required for applicants whose native language is not English and who did not receive a bachelor’s or master’s degree from an institution where the sole language of instruction is English.

Academic Transcripts (unofficial for the application, official required upon admission), three Letters of Recommendation submitted by your recommenders through the online application system, Resume/CV, Statement of Academic Purpose (an essay of approximately 500 words describing your academic and research experience, interests, and objectives), GRE General Test scores are required, GRE Subject Test scores are highly recommended, English Language Proficiency Requirement (for international applicants who are not citizens of certain English-speaking countries, did not complete their undergraduate or master’s degree at an institution where the sole language of instruction is English, or who are not applying to specific language programs where English proficiency is inherent to the curriculum).

A completed online application. Application fee. Academic transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended. Two letters of recommendation. Audition/Portfolio: Composition Portfolio: Upload a portfolio of 3-5 of your most representative scores and recordings directly to the online application. MIDI realizations are acceptable if live recordings are not available. Scores for works with recorded excerpts should be provided as one PDF file. Works for which scores are not available (e.g., electronic works) may be represented by recorded excerpts alone. Recordings of ensemble works may be submitted in audio or video format (audio preferred). All scores should clearly represent the applicant's original work. Short Composition Prompts: Please submit one example of a short composition prompt: Re-harmonize the melody and bassline of “I’ll Be Home For Christmas” (Lead Sheet is available here: https://steinhardt.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/2023-08/I%27ll%20Be%20Home%20for%20Christmas%20-%20Lead%20Sheet.pdf ) Using the melody and given bassline, create a new arrangement for a jazz quartet (piano, bass, drums, guitar, saxophone, or similar instrumentation). Use at least three of the suggested instruments in your score and recording. The arrangement must be 1-2 minutes in length. Submit a recording of your arrangement via YouTube or SoundCloud link. This recording can be a MIDI realization but must be well-produced. Submit a PDF of your score that includes piano and bass, plus three additional instruments. GRE not required.

Requirements: Applicants to the MA in Medical Humanities and Bioethics program must meet the general requirements for admission to GSAS. Candidates should hold a bachelor’s degree in a related field, though applicants with backgrounds in natural sciences, humanities, and social sciences are welcome. Required application materials include: a Statement of Purpose, three letters of recommendation, official transcripts from each college or university attended, and a non-refundable application fee ($85). The GRE General Test results are strongly recommended; applicants with strong academic records may request a waiver from the Director of Graduate Studies. English Language Proficiency is required for all international applicants unless they meet specific exemption criteria. Unofficial transcripts are uploaded with the application, with official transcripts required upon admission and matriculation. The Statement of Purpose should provide a clear and concise picture of academic and research interests.

Applicants must apply to the Graduate School of Arts and Science for a certificate program. The GRE General Test is required. An English Language Proficiency requirement applies for non-native English speakers.

Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to graduate study at NYU Tandon School of Engineering. Please submit the following documents with your application: A resume or CV, A statement of purpose, Three (3) letters of recommendation, Official transcripts for all higher education institutions attended, Official GRE scores (if applicable, see below), Official TOEFL/IELTS/PTE Academic scores (if applicable, see below), Optional: Any other documents you wish to include. A four-year bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. A strong background in science, including a full year of college-level physics and mathematics (including calculus). Other recommended courses include anatomy and physiology, biology, and chemistry. Experience in a clinical setting is preferred, but not required. International applicants must meet additional requirements as outlined by the Office of Graduate Admissions.

Applicants must apply online to the Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS) and submit required materials through the online application portal. They are neither required nor considered in the review process; English language proficiency examination scores (for non-native English speakers).

We will contact you directly if an interview is requested.)

All applicants for graduate programs at NYU Steinhardt must apply through the Steinhardt Graduate Admissions Application. When applying, be sure to upload the following items:
Unofficial transcripts from all colleges/universities you have attended are required for the application review. If admitted, official transcripts will be required.
Two letters of recommendation are required.
In one to two pages, describe your academic and professional qualifications, interests, and objectives related to the program. Indicate how our faculty and resources would assist you in achieving your goals. For students applying to both the Music Business MA and the JD/MA program, please be sure to address your interest in both degrees.
A résumé or curriculum vitae (CV) is required. Please include all relevant academic and work experience.
GRE scores are not required for this program. International students who are required to submit TOEFL/IELTS/PTE/Duolingo scores should refer to English Language Proficiency Testing Requirements.
A non-refundable application fee of $85.00 is required.

The MA in Music Education program requires the following: Online Application, Application Fee, Academic Transcripts, Two Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose: Your statement of purpose should be 2-3 pages, double-spaced. Please describe your professional goals, any significant teaching, leadership, or performance experiences, and how the MA in Music Education program will help you achieve your goals. Your statement should clearly indicate whether you are applying for the Initial Certification (for students who do not have prior teaching certification) or Professional Certification (for students who already hold teaching certification) path. GRE General Test: The GRE General Test is optional for Fall 2024 applicants to the Music Education MA. If you believe your GRE scores strengthen your application, you may submit them. If you do not submit GRE scores, your application will be reviewed without them. There is no minimum score requirement, and successful applicants typically have a balance of strong verbal, quantitative, and analytical writing scores. NYU Steinhardt's GRE code is 2599. English Language Proficiency, Resume/CV: Please include all work experience, particularly any teaching and/or performing experience. Audition: All applicants are required to complete an audition. If you reside within 150 miles of New York City, you must complete an in-person audition. If you reside beyond 150 miles of New York City, you may submit a video audition via the online application. In-person Audition Requirements (select your primary instrument/voice for specific repertoire) Brass Composition Guitar (Classical, Jazz) Percussion Piano (Classical, Jazz) Strings (Classical, Jazz) Voice (Classical, Jazz) Woodwinds Video Audition Requirements (same repertoire requirements as in-person) New York State Initial or Professional Teaching Certification: If you are applying for the Professional Certification path and already hold teaching certification, please upload a copy of your New York State Initial or Professional teaching certification. If you are applying for the Initial Certification path, this document is not required.

All applicants to graduate programs in Music must submit the following materials: Online Application, Application Fee, Academic Transcripts, Two letters of recommendation from individuals qualified to assess your academic potential, scholarly ability, and/or professional promise, A current resume or CV describing your academic, professional, and performance experience, A 1-2 page essay describing your academic and professional objectives and how they align with your interest in your program of study at NYU Steinhardt. Standardized Tests: The GRE General Test is not required for applicants to any graduate program in Music at NYU Steinhardt. English Language Proficiency Test (if applicable). For Music Education (MM, MM w/ Cert, PhD, Advanced Cert): Applicants must submit a separate artistic statement of no more than 500 words and schedule a brief interview with a faculty member via Zoom. This interview is not an audition.

Official transcripts from each post-secondary institution you have attended. Three letters of recommendation. A statement of purpose. A professional resume or curriculum vitae. Submit a resume or curriculum vitae listing your education, experience, honors, and other qualifications. Writing Sample: Required. Students apply online and will be notified of their admissions status approximately one to two weeks following the submission of their application. Application Requirements: A brief (300-500 words) personal statement outlining why you are interested in pursuing this particular certificate, how you hope it will help you achieve your professional goals, and what you will bring to the program. Upload a current resume or C.V. Submit unofficial transcripts from all prior higher education institutions. There is a non-refundable $75 application fee that must be submitted with your application.

Requirements: All applicants for admission to graduate study at NYU Steinhardt must submit the following materials electronically: Application, Application fee, Academic transcripts, Two letters of recommendation from faculty or employers who can speak to your academic and professional qualifications, a one- to two-page Statement of Purpose addressing your professional goals, experiences, and interest in our program, and a Resume/CV. The Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) are not required for admission to this program. Applicants are required to submit proof of English language proficiency if they did not complete their entire undergraduate degree (or master's degree) at an institution where the sole language of instruction was English. Music Therapy (MA) applicants must demonstrate sufficient music proficiency by submitting an audition via a recorded video or by a live in-person audition. Competitive applicants will be invited for an interview in February or March following the application deadline.

To apply for the Master of Arts in Music Therapy program, please submit the following via the Steinhardt Graduate Application: Application, Application Fee, Transcripts, Recommendations (two letters), Statement of Purpose, Resume/CV, Audition, Interview, GRE General Test (Not required), TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo English Test (Required for applicants who do not meet the waiver criteria).
Program name: Music Therapy MM with Undergraduate Equivalency

Requirements: Admission to the M.M. program in Musicology is for the fall semester only. Applicants are expected to have a strong undergraduate record and adequate preparation in music history. The GRE is not required. Required Application Materials: Statement of Purpose, Three Letters of Recommendation, Academic Transcripts, Writing Sample, Curriculum Vitae/Resume. Optional: GRE Scores (General and/or Subject Test).

Additionally, a writing sample, preferably a scholarly paper (20-25 pages), should be uploaded. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) general test is not required for applicants to the PhD program in Music.

All applicants to the Graduate School of Arts and Science (GSAS) are required to submit a completed online application, a statement of academic purpose, a resume or curriculum vitae (CV), and unofficial transcripts from each college or university attended. Letters of Recommendation: Three required. Transcripts: Unofficial transcripts are required for the application. Official transcripts are required upon admission.

All applicants must apply online through the GSAS Application. You may apply for admission for fall only. The deadline for receipt of all application materials is December 15. The Department does not admit students for Spring semester. Applications must include: Application Fee, Statement of Purpose, Writing Sample (not to exceed 5,000 words, including footnotes), Three Letters of Recommendation, All previous post-secondary transcripts, Resume/CV. GRE Scores are optional. Applicants for admission to the Philosophy PhD program who are not native speakers of English must present evidence of their proficiency in English by taking the TOEFL or IELTS examination.

Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Specific coursework is required and must be completed prior to matriculation. The admissions committee looks for applicants who have achieved strong grades, particularly in their science coursework. Additional Application Requirements for All Applicants: Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Two letters of recommendation (one from a science professor and one from a licensed physical therapist); A personal statement explaining your career goals and interest in physical therapy. Any updates will be posted on the program website. Applicants must meet the general requirements for admission to the Graduate School of Arts and Science and have a Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) degree (or equivalent). Three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required for admission to this program. Applicants with international degrees must demonstrate English proficiency.

Applicants are generally required to follow the application requirements set by the GSAS. Most importantly, the program is looking for a Statement of Purpose, three letters of recommendation, and transcripts from all previous universities attended. While the GSAS does not require the GRE General Test, applicants are strongly recommended to take it, as the application may be stronger with a high score. The GRE Physics Subject Test is highly encouraged but not required. An academic writing sample is asked for, if available, and can be submitted to admissions@physics.nyu.edu. All applicants are required to submit transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, and most are required to submit three letters of recommendation. All recommendation letters must be submitted online directly through the application system. Applicants must demonstrate proficiency in English unless they meet exemption criteria. A resume or CV can be a helpful supplement to the application.

The deadline for fall applications is December 15. The Department of Physics only accepts applications for fall admission. To apply, you should complete a brief online application, including your transcripts, a list of courses taken, and a curriculum vitae (CV). You will also be asked to provide a statement of purpose outlining your research interests and career goals. We also require three letters of recommendation from faculty members who know you well and can comment on your academic and research abilities. All application materials, including transcripts, letters, and scores, should be sent to the NYU GSAS Admissions Office. GRE General Test and GRE Physics Subject Test scores are not required for admission to the Physics PhD program.

Required Application Materials: Statement of Purpose, Resume or CV, Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, English Language Proficiency (if applicable). This should demonstrate your ability to teach in a popular music setting. The submission should be no longer than 15 minutes and include: A performance of two contrasting popular music pieces (e.g., different styles, tempos, or instrumentation). The performance can be solo, with accompaniment, or with a band. A short (3-5 minute) video demonstrating your teaching philosophy or approach in a popular music context (e.g., teaching a skill, discussing curriculum, etc.). Please provide context for your submission (e.g., a brief written description of the pieces, teaching demonstration, and rationale). Academic Writing Sample: Applicants must submit an academic writing sample, such as an excerpt from a research paper, an essay, or a critical review, demonstrating their ability to write clearly and analytically on a topic relevant to popular music or music education. The sample should be no longer than 10 pages.

Requirements: Admission to the Program Evaluation Advanced Certificate is highly selective. Students admitted to the certificate program typically have: A strong academic record with at least a 3.0 GPA; At least two years of full-time professional or other relevant experience for the online program. Students in any graduate degree program at NYU or any other institution, current students in the Steinhardt MS Program in Applied Psychology, or applicants with a master's degree (or higher) are also eligible to apply. Students who have previously completed graduate-level coursework related to program evaluation may be able to transfer up to 6 credits towards the certificate requirements. Please reach out to your academic advisor to determine eligibility. Required Application Materials: Transcripts from all undergraduate and graduate institutions attended, Letters of Recommendation (Two required), CV or Resume, Statement of Purpose, Application Fee, GRE General Test or LSAT or GMAT (not required for NYU Steinhardt graduate students), English Language Proficiency Test (if applicable).

Prerequisites for Admission: A master of science degree in nursing (MSN) or a doctor of nursing practice degree (DNP) from an accredited institution. (Post-baccalaureate DNP students are not eligible to apply for advanced certificates.) Current, unencumbered registered nurse (RN) license in the United States. Current, unencumbered advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) license in the United States in the specialty area in which the applicant is currently practicing, if applicable. National board certification as an advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) in the specialty area in which the applicant is currently practicing, if applicable. Minimum 3.0 GPA from prior master's or doctoral nursing program. Evidence of completion of graduate-level coursework in advanced pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and advanced health assessment. For PMHNP, prior graduate-level coursework in foundational primary care (e.g., adult, family) may also be required. Evidence of current clinical practice as an APRN in the specialty area for which you are seeking an advanced certificate or documented evidence of graduate-level clinical practice. PMHNP: Current, unencumbered APRN license in the US, and national certification as a Family, Adult, or Adult-Gerontology Nurse Practitioner, Clinical Nurse Specialist, or Certified Nurse Midwife (CNM). Additionally, applicants for the PMHNP Advanced Certificate program must submit evidence of a minimum of 500 supervised clinical hours (post-graduation from a master's or doctoral program) as an APRN and a copy of the supervising preceptor’s CV/resume along with an employment verification letter. Application Checklist: The following items are required for your application to be reviewed. Submit all materials directly through the online application portal unless otherwise specified. Online Application, Application Fee, Official Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, Current Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume, Statement of Professional Goals (approximately 500-750 words), Proof of valid, unencumbered RN License (New York State preferred, but not required for admission), Proof of valid, unencumbered APRN License and national board certification in your current advanced practice specialty, if applicable. Three Letters of Recommendation (at least one from a former faculty member and one from a current supervisor who can speak to your clinical aptitude), PMHNP Advanced Certificate applicants only: Preceptor CV/Resume, Employment Verification Letter, and Documented Evidence of 500 Supervised Clinical Hours.

Online Application. A current professional resume or CV. A Statement of Purpose, no more than 500 words, that explains your motivation for pursuing an MPA degree at NYU Wagner. Online Application, Resume or CV, Statement of Purpose, Official Transcripts, Two Letters of Recommendation, GRE Scores (Optional): While GRE scores are not a required component of the application, applicants may submit their scores if they feel they will strengthen their candidacy. Applicants to the NYU School of Global Public Health’s MPH program must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. The NYU School of Global Public Health has waived the GRE requirement for all Master of Public Health (MPH) applicants for the 2024-2025 application cycle. Scores are valid for five years.
